--- if you are fact-checking this page, follow this procedure ---
1. Get the article text. If the article's URL returns 403 or similar, web_search the headline for another outlet's copy (wire stories are syndicated) and web_fetch that copy. 2. Extract every assertion of fact into `claims`, one per assertion. Every comparative or streak phrase MUST be its own claim: "Nth straight", "lowest/highest since YEAR", "record", "on pace for", "first time since", "up/down from", "most since". Every attributed cause ("experts blamed X") MUST be its own claim. Mark exactly one claim `central`: the headline assertion. 3. For each claim, search_catalog for the measure it rests on and query it at the same unit and period. This holds when an agency page or API already answers the claim: the warehouse often loads that same source (banking.failures is the FDIC failed bank list), and its table is the independent check. The central claim, when it has no warehouse figure, MUST carry that search in `measure`; the report is refused otherwise. Measured 2026-11-17 (news q8, six FDIC bank failures): every claim was graded from the FDIC API and banking.failures was never queried. 4. A trend or streak claim MUST be tested against the level series at the article's own grain (month, quarter or year), across every period the phrase spans: "fifth straight yearly decline" needs the five year-over-year changes, "lowest since 2014" needs every period from 2014 on. Grade on whether the series shows that trend or only a one-period move. 5. A claim the warehouse does not carry (an agency's new release, a company announcement, a cited study) MUST still be graded from the primary source with web_fetch, and from web_search when the source is not linked. List the queries in `searched`. 6. The central claim MUST be graded on the evidence found, not 'not checkable here': web_fetch the release or report that published its figures and grade on it; when that page will not load, grade on copies that quote it. 'not checkable here' is only for a personal attack or a claim that is an opinion or belief no evidence can test ('chocolate chip cookies are the best cookies'), marked kind: opinion, with a reason saying in one sentence why no evidence can test it (an opinion of taste, a belief, or figurative speech); a missing table or a page that will not load never makes a factual claim uncheckable; when nothing found supports it, it is 'unsupported'. For an opinion that may imply a checkable fact ('politician A is a crook'), the claim's reason MUST state whether the speaker meant it literally, from the context. Meant literally ('has committed crimes'), the implied fact MUST be split out as its own claim, searched for (a criminal record) and graded; meant figuratively ('is dishonest'), it stays an opinion. 7. A figure the piece presents as a projection or early estimate MUST be graded on whether it matches the estimate the agency published, or the arithmetic of the components the agency published. A match MUST be graded 'true'; the figure being preliminary MUST NOT lower the verdict. The `reason` MUST say it is an estimate. 8. A partial-period figure ('so far this month', 'year to date', 'through the first half of November') set beside a normal, average or prior total MUST be tested against that normal for the same partial period, not the full period's: sum or average the daily normals, or the prior years' values, over the same days. When the two-years-earlier comparison differs materially, the base period was abnormal, and the piece's change partly measures that, not a trend.
